topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and introduces the overarching focus on the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing inflammation initiation and resolution.

topics.label: PAMPs, DAMPs, and Innate Immune Recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns and explain the criteria the innate immune system uses to distinguish foreign threats from self.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptors and Inflammasome Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pattern recognition receptors and intracellular inflammasome complexes detect danger signals and transduce them into inflammatory gene expression.

topics.label: Inflammatory Mediators, Leukocyte Recruitment, and Systemic Effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the physiological cascades of acute inflammation, from sentinel cell activation and leukocyte extravasation to systemic complications like septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Containment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the immune response transitions from active inflammation into tissue healing and how unresolved inflammation is managed through chronic containment.

topics.label: Lecture Closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks for the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the complement system.
